rows.note: Use 淹沒 as the all-purpose choice when someone or something is figuratively overwhelmed or literally submerged.

example.english: Huge waves can engulf the whole beach.
example.traditional: 大浪可以淹沒成個海灘。
example.jyutping: daai6 long6 ho2 ji5 jim1 mut6 sing4 go3 hoi2 taan1

rows.note: Use 包圍 specifically when engulf means surrounding something without necessarily covering or submerging it.

example.english: A large group of reporters began to engulf the singer, leaving him unable to move.
example.traditional: 一大班記者喺門口包圍住個歌手，搞到佢行唔到。
example.jyutping: jat1 daai6 baan1 gei3 ze2 hai2 mun4 hau2 baau1 wai4 zyu6 go3 go1 sau2 gaau2 dou3 keoi5 haang4 m4 dou3

rows.note: Use 籠罩 when a depressive mood or other powerful feeling hangs over and overwhelms someone.

example.english: Grief over losing a loved one continued to engulf him, making it hard for him to recover.
example.traditional: 親人離世嘅悲痛一直籠罩住佢，令佢好耐都振作唔到。
example.jyutping: can1 jan4 lei4 sai3 ge3 bei1 tung3 jat1 zik6 lung5 zaau3 zyu6 keoi5 ling6 keoi5 hou2 noi6 dou1 zan3 zok3 m4 dou3
